title: Stańczyk
altText: A man in a jester's costume sits apart from a lively party in a grand room, looking serious and thoughtful. In the background, other people dance and celebrate.

source.verifiedBy: arthistoryproject.com artwork page text (title, year, medium, collection, public-domain statement)

context: An oil painting by Jan Matejko, a Polish painter, made in 1862. It shows Stanczyk, a court jester remembered in Polish history. The source page tags it Clowns. Matejko painted many scenes from Polish history.

descriptions.k: A man in a jester costume sits alone. He is not laughing. Behind him, people are at a big party. Why do you think he looks so serious? What is he thinking about?
descriptions.g12: Jan Matejko painted Stanczyk, a court jester. A jester usually makes people laugh. But this jester sits apart and looks serious while a party goes on behind him. What do you think he is thinking about, and what do you see that tells you?
descriptions.g35: Jan Matejko painted Stanczyk in 1862 in Poland. Stanczyk was a court jester, a person who entertained a royal court. Here he sits away from a lively party and looks thoughtful. Look at his face, his costume, and the people behind him. How does the painter show that he is different from the party?
descriptions.g68: In Stanczyk (1862), Matejko shows a court jester sitting apart from a festive gathering, absorbed in serious thought. Jesters were meant to amuse, which makes his mood surprising. The party continues behind him, creating a contrast. What does the difference between foreground and background suggest about his role, and what questions does the painting raise?
descriptions.g910: Matejko's Stanczyk (1862) turns a figure of entertainment into a figure of reflection. The jester sits in the foreground, withdrawn, while the festivities continue in the background. By setting thought against celebration, Matejko invites viewers to consider the role of a person who may see more than others. How do composition and contrast shape your interpretation of his mood and meaning?
descriptions.g1112: Stanczyk (1862) reverses expectations: the court jester, a figure associated with laughter, appears solitary and absorbed while a festive scene unfolds behind him. Painted by Matejko, a Polish history painter, it has been read as a meditation on duty, awareness, and the burden of insight, among other interpretations. How do spatial arrangement and contrast support or complicate such readings?

teacherNote.context: An 1862 oil painting by Jan Matejko showing Stanczyk, a court jester of Polish memory, apart from a festive scene. The source page tags it Clowns.
directions: Ask students to write the thoughts Stanczyk might have, using clues from the picture.
Discuss the difference between telling jokes and noticing what is going on around you.
Compare how a painter and a photographer might show a person who feels apart from a crowd.
